newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola reaches agreement on Surge name.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola reaches agreement on Surge name.

text.p: Babson Bros Co, a privately-held producer of milking machines and cleansers, said Thursday it reached a trademark settlement with Coca-Cola Co, allowing the beverage giant to launch its new Surge soft drink during Sunday's Super Bowl.

"We have satisfactorily resolved our differences with Coca-Cola and we have taken steps to avoid any potential confusion in the marketplace, thereby protecting the integrity, trust and distinctiveness of our flagship brand with our customers," Nick Babson, Naperville, Ill.-based Babson Bros. chairman, said in a statement.
Specific terms of the agreement were not disclosed.

Coca-Cola planned to launch the high-caffeine, lime-colored Surge as a competitor to Mountain Dew soft drink made by its rival PepsiCo Inc with a $50 million advertising campaign beginning during the Super Bowl on Sunday.

Babson contended that it had held a trademark on the name Surge since 1925 for its automatic milking machine and industrial cleaning products. The company was concerned there might be a health risk if consumers confused its green-colored cleaning products with the new soft drink, which Babson referred to as a "fully loaded" citrus-flavored soda.
Babson originally filed the trademark infringement suit in U.S. District Court in Chicago on Dec. 23.
